page.overview:
Who is Kteatus?

Kteatus and his brother Eurytus were twin brothers in Greek Mythology. Named the Moliones or Molionidai for their mother, Molione, they were the sons of either Aktor or Poseidon and nephew of Augeas. Greek legend maintains that the brothers were born conjoined with only one body but two heads, four arms and four legs, Homer however does not make mention of this.

Kteatus was one of the Kalydonian Hunters. His exact role of Kteatus in the hunt is unknown.

Both brothers went on expeditions of war to the Neleus and the Pylians, and later led an army marching against their uncle Augeas at the request of Herakles. After the brothers had finally appeared to have made peace with Herakles, they attacked Herakles and were subsequently killed by him outside Kleonae.

Kteates married Therenike one of the twin daughters of Dexamenus. Kteatus' son was Amphimachus, were counted among the Akhaean leaders in the Trojan War.
